input: Shop for a new road bicycle under budget

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: The exact budget ceiling determines which bike models, brands, and component tiers are realistically on the table — the entire product search space shifts dramatically between $500 and $3000.
Road cycling covers very different disciplines (endurance, racing, gravel, commuting) and knowing the intended use narrows geometry, gearing, and tyre clearance requirements significantly.
Rider dimensions (height, inseam) and experience level affect which frame sizes and component setups are appropriate, and whether a beginner or performance-oriented spec is right.
Where the bike will be ridden (terrain, road quality, distance) and how often changes recommendations around frame material, gearing range, and tyre width.
Whether the user wants to buy online, visit a local bike shop, or both affects where to direct the search and whether a test ride is part of the process.
Priorities like frame material (carbon vs aluminium), brand loyalty, weight, or aesthetics can override pure value-for-money logic and must be surfaced early.
Knowing what 'done well' looks like — lowest price found, best spec-per-dollar, a bike that fits perfectly, or a purchase made by a specific date — determines how to evaluate options.

gold.taskTitle: Shop for a new road bicycle under budget
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to research and purchase a new road bicycle while staying within a budget they have in mind.

questions.title: What is your exact maximum budget for this bike?
questions.description: Establish the hard spending ceiling so that the entire search can be scoped to realistic price tiers and no unsuitable options are surfaced.

questions.title: What will you primarily use this road bike for?
questions.description: Determine the main riding purpose — weekend fitness rides, competitive racing, long-distance touring, or daily commuting — to guide geometry and component choices.

questions.title: What is your height and current cycling experience level?
questions.description: Capture rider physical dimensions and skill background to recommend the correct frame size and whether a performance or entry-level spec is appropriate.

questions.title: What kind of roads and terrain will you ride on most?
questions.description: Understand whether the rider will be on smooth tarmac, rough chip-seal, mixed surfaces, or hilly routes to inform tyre width, gearing range, and frame stiffness needs.

questions.title: Do you prefer to buy online or visit a local bike shop?
questions.description: Clarify the preferred purchasing channel to direct the search appropriately and factor in whether a test ride, professional fitting, or assembly service is expected.

questions.title: Do you have any strong preferences on frame material or brand?
questions.description: Surface any non-negotiable preferences around carbon vs aluminium, specific brands, weight targets, or aesthetics that would override a purely value-based recommendation.

questions.title: Is there a deadline by which you need the bike ready to ride?
questions.description: Identify whether there is a target date — a race, a trip, or a season start — that constrains how quickly a decision must be made and limits options to in-stock availability.
